localBiteReport: The most recent readable reports with direct Choctawhatchee Bay content are from late October through early November 2026 (roughly 2–4 weeks old), so treat this as a recent baseline rather than a same-week update. Capt. Blake Nelson of Last Cast Charters (Freeport/Destin area) reported that the redfish bite on Choctawhatchee Bay flats remained productive heading into fall, with fish in the 23-inch-and-under range holding in guts, potholes, and shallow feeding areas; cut mullet on Carolina rigs outperformed live bait on some days. The broader northwest Florida picture for the week of November 13–19 showed bull redfish continuing to hold reliably around passes and bridge structure, while trout and sheepshead were picking up as water temperatures cooled. A FishingBooker charter review from about one week ago mentioned two solid redfish caught on a Choctawhatchee Bay trip that also fished under a bridge. Water temp on the bay today is 70°F.
